reviewed_by: Claude review of harness connection recovery
reason: Six verified defects in the harness runtime left a session stuck after a vendor process misbehaved. (1) HarnessRuntimeService._connection returned the cached connection whenever the browser binding matched and never consulted connection_state, and stream_turn's generic except marked the turn INTERRUPTED but kept the dead connection cached, so after a Codex/Grok process died mid-turn every later turn on that session wrote to the dead _CodexRpc/_AcpRpc and failed forever; _CodexRpc._reader also let a ValueError from readline() end the reader while the process stayed alive, so the next request() awaited a future nobody resolves. _connection now discards a connection whose connection_state is 'disconnected' the same way it handles a browser-binding change (new _discard_connection helper closes it, drops it and its gateway), stream_turn discards the connection when the failure is a HarnessTransportError/OSError, and _CodexRpc._end_transport marks the transport closing, fails pending futures, kills a still-live process, and _write refuses new requests on a closed transport. (2) connection.interrupt() was awaited with no timeout at shutdown, stop, cancel_turn (twice) and both stream_turn interrupt sites; Codex answers it as an RPC request and Grok's notify blocks on stdin.drain, so a wedged vendor hung Stop and Core shutdown and held _active and the session lock. Every site now goes through _interrupt_connection, which bounds the call with HARNESS_INTERRUPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (5 s), records a diagnostic on timeout and falls back to closing and forgetting the connection. (3) GrokAcpConnection.run_turn set active=True before awaiting session/set_mode outside the try/finally, so a rejected mode left active True and every later turn raised 'already has an active turn'; ClaudeAgentSdkConnection.run_turn had the same shape around client.query. Both now set active only after the pre-turn await succeeds. (4) ClaudeAgentSdkAdapter.open had no HARNESS_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS wrapper unlike Codex and Grok, so client.connect() could block forever holding the session lock; CodexAppServerAdapter.list_external_sessions issued initialize and up to ten thread/list requests with no deadline while probe bounds them at 15 s. Claude open now wraps _open in asyncio.timeout like the others; the Codex listing bounds each call with CODEX_SESSION_LIST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and raises HarnessUnavailableError on timeout. (5) GrokAcpAdapter.list_external_sessions did not kill or wait the `grok sessions list` child when communicate() timed out, leaking one live grok process per GET external-sessions; it now kills and waits before raising, matching _grok_model_catalog. (6) stream_turn's generic except called _fail_turn but never interrupted the vendor turn, so a Nebula-side error mid-stream left Codex/Claude executing with no consumer; it now interrupts (bounded) before failing the turn. New tests, each failing on main: test_harnesses.py::test_transport_loss_discards_the_dead_connection_before_the_next_turn, ::test_next_turn_reopens_a_connection_that_reports_disconnected, ::test_stop_closes_a_connection_that_never_acknowledges_interrupt, ::test_nebula_side_failure_mid_stream_interrupts_the_vendor_turn; test_harness_adapters.py::test_grok_connection_stays_usable_after_a_rejected_mode, ::test_claude_connection_clears_active_when_the_query_is_rejected, ::test_claude_open_is_bounded_by_the_startup_deadline, ::test_codex_session_listing_is_bounded_when_the_app_server_stalls, ::test_grok_session_listing_timeout_kills_the_child_process, ::test_codex_rpc_reader_limit_overrun_ends_the_transport. The rest of test_harnesses.py, test_harness_adapters.py and test_harness_connection_state.py cover the surrounding stop/cancel, browser-binding reopen, reader and connection_state behaviour that these paths share.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (the real-Core journey suite matched through harnesses.py) does not exercise a vendor process dying mid-turn, a hung interrupt, or a stalled sessions listing; the Python tests drive these paths directly with fake transports and a sleeping child process. No full suites.
